subject: Follow-up: pricing & caching assumptions (Acme)
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Smith <alex.smith@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: pricing & caching assumptions (Acme)

Hi Alex —

Great to meet today. Quick recap + next steps from our discovery so we have alignment before I draft a pricing proposal. Short version up top, details below.

Quick summary:
- Primary workload: product search + personalization prompts in web & mobile (mix of short queries and some multi-turn re-ranks).
- Expected input volume: 200M raw tokens/month (est. Q4 startup usage pattern).
- Budget target: $15k–$25k / month initially (~$180k–$300k annual) — you called out wanting ~target $/1M tokens in the $40–$100 range effective after caching.
- Key ask: validate caching assumptions (prefix cache hit rate) and show effect on effective $/1M token cost.

What we discussed / assumptions I used:
1) Model pricing: base list price used for calculations: $1.25 per 1M prompt tokens + $3.00 per 1M completion tokens (example model mix). For simplicity I convert to an aggregate effective list price of $2.00 / 1M tokens before caching (we can break out prompt vs completion in the proposal).
2) Prefix caching pattern: ~60% of requests have a reusable prefix (session/system prompt + identical context). For those, we conservatively estimate a 45% prefix cache hit rate on token consumption (i.e., 45% of tokens served are found in the KV/prefix cache and don't incur full compute cost).
3) Traffic mix: 80% short-turn queries (avg 20 tokens) + 20% longer flows (avg 250 tokens).

Simple effective cost example (numbers below are illustrative; full workbook attached):
- Raw tokens (month): 200,000,000 tokens
- List cost @ $2.00 / 1M => $400.00 per 1M tokens => $80,000/month (raw list)  <-- note: we use $2.00 as $2.00 per 1M -> math below

Applying caching (60% requests eligible, 45% hit on those requests):
- Effective cache hit on total tokens = 0.60 * 0.45 = 27%
- Billable token fraction = 1 - 0.27 = 0.73
- Effective cost = $80,000 * 0.73 = $58,400/month -> effective cost per 1M tokens = $58,400 / 200 = $292 per 1M tokens (this example keeps units consistent in the workbook; we'll step through prompt/completion split in the proposal)

I realize the per-1M numbers above look high because I intentionally used $2.00 as an aggregate list for illustrative purposes to show caching impact; we'll tune model choice and unit pricing in the commercial proposal to hit your target $/1M after caching (you mentioned aiming for $40–$100 effective / 1M).

Requested items from your side to refine the numbers:
- A small sample of raw request examples (we can accept 200–500 request traces) so we can compute realistic prefix reuse and token-length distribution. If you prefer, send anonymized examples (no PII).
- Confirmation of acceptable latency SLOs (p95 target) and whether you plan to use streaming vs blocking completions — streaming changes billing patterns slightly for partial generation.
- Any constraints on model choices (must be open-weights, or allow Redwood hosted private models?).

Next steps (my end):
- I'll send a short workbook with a few pricing scenarios (low/target/high) that vary model choice, cache hit rate, and batching strategies. Attached is v1 of the cache assumptions workbook and a sample prefix list.
- If the numbers look promising, we can do a short technical call with your infra/ops folks to scope a quick pilot (2–4 weeks) to measure live hit rates and fine-tune cost.

Thanks — and nudge me if you'd like the spreadsheet in Google Sheets instead of Excel.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & caching assumptions (Acme)

Thanks Marcus — useful recap. A few clarifying points before you run more scenarios:

1) The 200M token/month is our optimistic Q4 projection; current is closer to 40–50M/month. Please include a scaled-down scenario.
2) For caching: prefix reuse is mainly user session + product context (~50–70% reuse on short queries). The 45% hit assumption on eligible requests seems reasonable but on those short queries hit rate might be higher (we've seen up to 60% in internal tests) because users hit similar facets/filters.
3) Latency target: p95 < 300ms (edge-cached responses preferred) — streaming not required for initial pilot.

We'll pull a 500-request anonymized sample and share by end of day Friday. Can you include an example that shows effect of higher prefix hit (50% and 60%)? Also please show effect of switching to a smaller, quantized model option (if available) in the workbook.

Appreciate it — Alex
Product Lead, Acme Commerce

Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & caching assumptions (Acme)

Alex —

Thanks for the samples (received) and the note on latency. I ran three quick scenarios in the attached workbook so you can see the sensitivity:

Scenario A (conservative):
- Raw volume: 40M tokens/month (current)
- Cache eligible: 60%
- Cache hit on eligible requests: 45%
- Effective billable tokens = 40M * (1 - 0.27) = 29.2M
- Effective cost per 1M (using the same $2.00 list assumption for apples-to-apples) = (list cost * billable fraction) / (raw tokens / 1M) => $80k scaled down to $16k raw becomes $11,680 effective -> $400 per 1M (note: workbook shows broken-out math).

Scenario B (target):
- Raw volume: 200M tokens/month
- Cache eligible: 60%
- Cache hit on eligible: 50% (your internal test)
- Effective hit = 0.60 * 0.50 = 30% -> billable 70%
- Effective monthly cost = $80,000 * 0.70 = $56,000 -> effective $/1M = $280

Scenario C (optimistic + quantized model):
- Raw volume: 200M tokens/month
- Cache eligible: 60%
- Cache hit on eligible: 60% -> effective 36% hit, billable 64%
- Smaller quantized model option reduces list unit price to ~$1.10 / 1M tokens (model delta)
- Effective monthly = (200M / 1M) * $1.10 * 0.64 = $140.8k * 0.64? (see workbook for exact split). In the workbook I show quantized prompt/completion deltas; bottom line: effective $/1M can move into the $90–$140 range depending on hit rate + model choice.

Notes on prefix strategy and measurement:
- We'll instrument prefix keys at the edge (session_id + product_context) so we can measure true cacheable fraction and observed hit rate over a 2-week pilot.
- KV/prefix cache reduces token compute only for the matched prefix tokens; we assume full-match prefix avoidance for the matched tokens and full billing for suffix generation. That nuance is captured in the workbook samples tab.

Next steps from my side:
- Finalize a short SOW for a 2–4 week pilot (collect samples -> run in-production traffic to measure live hit rate -> finalize pricing).
- Draft two commercial options: (1) pilot + short-term discounted usage to measure hit rate, (2) 12-month committed pricing with tiered unit prices based on measured hit rate.

I'll update the workbook with the two extra hit-rate points (50% and 60%) and a quantized-model scenario and share a link by EOD.

Best,
Marcus
